input.question: why does renting a movie digitally cost so much more (usually 4-5 dollars) than renting a physical disc from a service like RedBox (usually 1-2 dollars)?
input.ground_truth: Simply a convenience fee. Also, movie companies charge a lot more for digital rights, as more people will stream/download them than buy the physical copy, that's why Netflix's physical library is much larger than their digital library.

Question: why does renting a movie digitally cost so much more (usually 4-5 dollars) than renting a physical disc from a service like RedBox (usually 1-2 dollars)?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you want to watch a fun movie.

When you rent a movie **from your TV or phone (digital)**, it’s like asking a store to send the movie straight to your house through magic internet wires. The store has to pay for the magic internet and make sure the movie gets to you without any problems. Also, they want to make sure you can watch it easily and that no one else can steal it. That’s why it costs more—because it’s a special way of sending the movie just for you.

When you rent a **DVD from a RedBox**, it’s like borrowing a toy from a box at the store. The store only needs to put the DVD in the box and take it back later. It doesn’t use the magic internet as much, and lots of people share the same DVDs. That’s why it’s cheaper.

So, digital renting costs more because it’s like having the movie come to you magically, and that takes more work and money. Renting a DVD is just borrowing a plastic disc from a nearby box, which is cheaper and easier for the store.
